title: 16-06-pace-code-c-2015.pdf — section 111
text:
1. A person shall always be invited to write down what they want to
say.

2. A person who has not been charged with, or informed they may be
prosecuted for, any offence to which the statement they want to
write relates, shall:
(a) unless the statement is made at a time when the
restriction on drawing adverse inferences from silence
applies, see Annex C, be asked to write out and sign the
following before writing what they want to say:
‘I make this statement of my own free will. I understand
that I do not have to say anything but if I do not mention
something which I later rely on in court it may harm my
defence. This statement may be given in evidence’;
(b) if the statement is made at a time when the restriction on
drawing adverse inferences from silence applies, be asked
to write out and sign the following before writing what
they want to say:
‘I make this statement of my own free will. I understand
that I do not have to say anything. This statement may be
given in evidence.’
